procedural_matters: ITA 257 was represented by Giulio Zezza (crew).
FRA 270 was represented by Felix Tron (helm).
Jerome Demange (FRA 270's coach) attended the hearing as an interpreter for FRA 270.
Vittoria Montevecchi (ITA 246's crew) gave evidence during the hearing as a witness for ITA 257.
ITA 257 did not ask to withdraw the protest after the arbitration meeting and neither boat took a Post-Race Penalty under RRS T1(a)].
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 15, gusting 17 knots of wind and steep waves.
ITA 257 was sailing on starboard tack, on the last downwind leg at a speed of 12-13 knots. FRA 270 was sailing on port tack on a collision course with ITA 257, at a speed of 14 knots.
When the boats were 7 boat lengths apart, ITA 257 was aiming 4 boat lengths in front of FRA 270's bow.
At that moment, ITA 257 eased both the mainsheet and gennaker sheet, and luffed slightly. FRA 270 held her course and crossed in front of ITA 257.
conclusions: There was reasonable doubt that FRA 270 could have crossed, if ITA 257 had not taken avoiding action (see WS Case 50).
FRA 270 on port tack failed to keep clear of ITA 257 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
